newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia beef prices improve - Dresdner/NFF.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia beef prices improve - Dresdner/NFF.

text.p: Beef prices showed an improvement during October because of increasing strength in the U.S. and Japanese markets, according to an international commodity price review released on Monday by the National Farmers' Federation (NFF) and Dresdner Australia Ltd.
The review shows beef prices increased by 0.9 percent during the month to bring them 12.4 percent above their low in June.

NFF director of economic policy Todd Ritchie said the price improvements were driven by a decline in beef production and the feed cattle slaughter rate in the United States, combined with an increase in Japanese consumer confidence.
"Renewed pressure on beef prices in our export markets may, however, come towards the end of the year as U.S. beef production picks up," Ritchie said.

Rural prices in special drawing rights (SDR) terms fell by 2.2 percent in October, but remain 7.8 percent higher than a year ago, he said. The fall in prices was led by barley, sorghum, wool and sugar, he said.
October had seen grain prices weaken, with an upward revision of world coarse grain production by the United States Department of Agriculture, he said.

Dresdner chief economist Rob Henderson said the SDR commodity price index increased by 0.6 percent in October, but remained 0.8 percent below the level of a year ago in Australian dollar termns because of a stronger A$ over the past 12 months.

The outlook for the world economy suggested that commodity prices overall could be slightly higher over the next six to nine months, which could see the A$ rise above 80 cents US in the first half of 1997, he said.
Non-rural SDR prices increased by 1.9 percent during October and are now 7.8 percent higher than 12 months ago, he said.
The rise was principally the result of energy prices strengthening further, he said.
